region: Tropical West, Central and East Africa
description: African mahogany is the trade name for several Khaya species, mainly K. ivorensis, K. anthotheca, K. grandifoliola and K. senegalensis. It is a pinkish to reddish-brown hardwood used as a lower-cost alternative to genuine mahogany for furniture, cabinetry, veneer, joinery and boat work.

hazards.summary: Furniture workers in two UK factories developed allergic skin rashes traced by patch testing to the dust of Khaya anthotheca. Affected workers reacted strongly to anthothecol, a natural compound in the wood.
Occupational asthma from Khaya anthotheca is listed in a peer-reviewed review of wood dust allergy, based on a German workplace study we have not yet been able to check directly.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nasal cavity and sinuses after long-term exposure.

known_compounds.name: anthothecol
known_compounds.role: contact allergen identified by patch testing in sensitized workers (K. anthotheca)

related_species_note: Khaya is in the same family (Meliaceae) as genuine mahogany (Swietenia) and sapele (Entandrophragma). Evidence from K. anthotheca may not apply equally to every Khaya species.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed African mahogany (Khaya ivorensis) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Heartwood a light pinkish-brown to pale reddish-brown, more muted and slightly paler than genuine mahogany, with the colour deepening toward the board's centre; sapwood a faint creamy band barely distinct from the heartwood. Interlocked grain that shows a soft ribbon stripe along the face, medium-coarse texture with open pores visible as fine streaks, a few patches of slightly fuzzy torn grain, and a moderate silky luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of African mahogany with light pinkish-brown heartwood and a soft ribbon stripe from interlocked grain.
notes_internal: No ACGIH A2 carcinogen entry added on purpose: OSHA-CSI lists 'mahogany' as A2 without a botanical name, and Haz-Map's wording linking it to Khaya is a lead only. Another agent is resolving which mahogany ACGIH means; add a level 2 carcinogen hazard and carcinogen_class here only if that resolution includes Khaya. HSE-WIS30 'Mahogany' is likewise not botanically specified and is not cited here. Asthma rests on Schlunssen-2018 Table 1 (K. anthotheca, citing Oertmann & Bergmann 1993, Allergologie 16:334-340, not indexed in PubMed).
